answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a market, then slash it when an independently verifiable dispute proves fraud. Creating a hundred fake identities no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up capital, and any identity caught cheating loses its stake. A dawn audit can sample claims linked in a thread, while yarrow marks the settlement window; the mechanism raises the attacker’s cost without assuming that names or reputation alone prove uniqueness.
